# The First Chapter {#sec-first}

This is the first page of the first chapter. You may delete the contents of this chapter
so you can add your own text; it's just here to show you some examples.

## References, Labels, Cross-references and Footnotes {#sec-references}

It is easy to refer to anything within your document. Give a heading, figure, table or
equation a label that starts with the right prefix (`sec-`, `fig-`, `tbl-` or `eq-`),
and refer to it with `@` followed by the label. Labels must be unique and shouldn't use
spaces or odd characters. Quarto keeps track of the chapter, section, figure and table
numbers, and even adds the word "Figure" or "Table" for you.

### References and labels

For example, @tbl-inheritance shows that many factors can be assumed to follow from
inheritance, and @fig-subd shows an image. You can also point back to sections: this
one is @sec-references, and the chapter on math is @sec-math.

### Custom shorthand

Are you tired of typing the same phrase over and over? For text, a small
[Quarto shortcode or variable](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/variables.html) works
in both PDF and Word. For LaTeX-only macros (PDF output), put `\newcommand` lines in
`header-includes` in `_quarto.yml`.

### Footnotes

You might want to footnote something.^[Footnote text goes right here, inside the
brackets.] The footnote is placed appropriately in both the PDF and Word output.

## Bibliographies {#sec-bib}

Of course you will need to cite things, and you will probably accumulate an armful of
sources. Put them in `references.bib` (BibTeX format; tools like Zotero or JabRef can
export it), then cite them by key. Put the key in square brackets to get a
parenthetical citation [@angel:2000], use `@angel:2000` for a text citation like
@angel:2000, and separate several keys with semicolons [@angel:2000; @deussen:2000].
You can also cite a website [@reedweb:2007] or a Reed thesis [@noble:2002].

The bibliography style is set once, in `_quarto.yml`: `bibstyle: apa` for the PDF and
`csl: csl/apa.csl` for Word. To use another style, change `bibstyle` (for example
`chicago` or `ieee`) and download the matching `.csl` file from the
[Zotero style repository](https://www.zotero.org/styles).

### Tips for bibliographies

1. Like with thesis formatting, the sooner you start compiling your bibliography for
   something as large as a thesis, the better. Do you really want to type in source
   after source in late April? Think of it as procrastination.
2. Each entry's key (its label) must be unique.
3. When there is more than one author or editor, separate names with the word "and":
   `author = {Noble, Sam and Youngberg, Jessica}`.
4. To force capitalization in an article title, put the capital letter in curly
   braces.
5. For a Reed thesis, use the `phdthesis` entry type and put "Reed thesis" or
   "Undergraduate thesis" in the optional `type` field.
